topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the topic of complement and sets expectations for the lecture.

topics.label: Complement fundamentals and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the overall structure, historical nomenclature, and central enzymatic role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct upstream pathways and threshold dynamics that drive complement activation on pathogen surfaces.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream biological actions through which activated complement eliminates pathogens.

topics.label: Host regulation and self-protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the molecular mechanisms and regulatory factors that prevent complement from destroying healthy host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how deficiencies in specific complement components result in distinct clinical diseases and immunopathologies.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how pathogens have evolved molecular strategies to overcome complement-mediated immunity, illustrated by Staphylococcus aureus.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the lecture on complement and announces the topic of the next session.
